description: Emit the compact move trace for one closed Wirth Sierpinski curve.

source.discovery_scope: Pinned title and score metadata only; no task text, examples, tests, or submissions used.
source.algorithm_description: Niklaus Wirth, Algorithms and Data Structures (Oberon version), Section 3.3, Figures 3.5-3.6, pp. 105-107.
source.variant: Benchmark order q denotes Wirth curve S_q. q=0 is the non-empty S0 base square; q=1 and q=2 are his first two refined curves. The path is A(q), outer direction 7, B(q), direction 5, C(q), direction 3, D(q), direction 1.

input.validation_order: Validate non-null input, exact length, and order before output pointer or capacity checks.

output.encoding: One move byte per line segment. Low 3 bits are Wirth's direction index (45 degrees times the value); bit 3 selects length 2h instead of h. No output header.

workspace.accounting: At most 64 fixed two-byte symbol/depth frames (128 bytes), plus order, stack/output indices, and scalar loop state. Input and output buffers are excluded.

complexity.primary: O(4^(q+1)) time for recursive A/B/C/D expansion; O(q) active recursion state, bounded by the fixed order range.
complexity.independent: O(4^(q+1)) time for grammar rewriting; O(4^(q+1)) temporary token storage in the Python reference. Native ports use a fixed expansion stack.
